member.summary: Convenience helper that bin-packs a list of mesh instances across one or more s. Each mesh's atlas footprint is sized from its world-space surface area times the texelsPerWorldUnit density squared (so larger surfaces get more lightmap resolution), then shelf-packed into atlases: when the current atlas runs out of room, a new one is created.

member.summary: Largest per-triangle world_area / uv_area ratio across every triangle in the mesh under the given transform. Returns 0 for empty or fully-degenerate meshes (callers clamp).

member.name: P:XEngine.Photonic.BakeOptions.UseHemisphereLUT
member.summary: When true, indirect bounce directions are drawn from a precomputed 16k-entry Halton-distributed cosine-hemisphere LUT (cheap, low-discrepancy). When false, each bounce builds a fresh direction via Malley's method (sqrt + sin/cos + sqrt). The LUT is the faster default; flip this off if you suspect it's causing visible structure in the lightmap from repeated directions.

member.name: P:XEngine.Photonic.BakeOptions.IncludeDirectLighting
member.summary: When true, the lightmap includes direct lighting at the texel itself (sun rays directly striking the surface being baked). When false, only the indirect contribution is stored: direct shadow rays at bounce hit points are still fired (so light bounced off other surfaces propagates correctly), but the texel's own direct lighting must be added at runtime by a dynamic-light shader. The standard "indirect-only baked lighting" pipeline.

member.name: P:XEngine.Photonic.BakeOptions.DoBackfaceCull

When false the tracer is two-sided (historic behavior). The front-face winding is fixed to the renderer's convention by the integrator.

member.name: T:XEngine.Photonic.Imaging.LightmapDenoiser
member.summary: Edge-avoiding a-trous wavelet denoiser for baked lightmaps. Smooths the Monte-Carlo noise left on a surface without bleeding across chart seams or geometric / lighting edges, by weighting each tap with the rasterizer's per-texel world position + normal guides. Operates on covered texels only, in linear HDR, and is meant to run once on the converged atlas just before the final dilation.
member.remarks: Each pass reads a frozen snapshot and writes a ping-pong buffer; rows are independent so the row loop runs through . The tap spacing doubles every pass (1, 2, 4, ...), so a handful of passes covers a wide kernel at a few taps each.

member.summary: Denoise (R,G,B interleaved HDR, length width*height*3) in place. / are the rasterizer's per-texel coverage + guides (row-major y*width + x). There is no radiance edge-stop: taps are weighted only by the geometric guides (same surface normal + same plane), so Monte-Carlo noise is averaged out regardless of magnitude (shadow edges on a flat surface soften as a result). Uncovered texels are left untouched for dilation.

member.name: T:XEngine.Photonic.Integration.BakeAcceleration
member.summary: The ray-tracing acceleration structure + pre-resolved material tables for a bake. Shared by the per-frame (lightmap texels) and (light probes) so both trace against an identical scene.
member.remarks:
Baking is static (nothing moves) and every surface is baked uniquely, so there's no need for a two-level TLAS-over-instances structure. Instead we bake all instances' triangles into a single world-space — one tight triangle-level BVH with no per-ray instance transform and no instance-AABB culling to defeat on overlapping geometry. Per-hit shading reads world position/normal/UV0 straight off the merged mesh; the merged material groups map 1:1 to .
The rasterizer keys texels by the source + its material group, so keeps per-instance material resolution for that path.

member.name: T:XEngine.Photonic.Integration.PathIntegrator
member.summary: CPU path tracer. Given a surface point with a normal and a material, returns the radiance arriving on that point from all lights (direct) plus indirect diffuse bounces.
member.remarks:
Direct: next-event estimation. For every light, sample one shadow ray; multiply by the material's diffuse albedo x dot(n, l).
Indirect: a small number of cosine-weighted bounces. With cosine sampling, the PDF is cos / π and the integrand brdf * cos / pdf = albedo. So each bounce just multiplies the carried throughput by the surface's diffuse albedo. Cheap and converges fast on diffuse scenes.
Material lookups are precomputed: callers pass resolvedMats[blasIndex][groupIndex] so the inner loop avoids the per-bounce FindMaterial dictionary hit.

member.summary: Direct + indirect irradiance at a surface point. The lightmap stores incoming light; the runtime shader multiplies by the surface's own diffuse texture at draw time. The texel's own parameter is therefore not applied here: only hit-surface albedos (one per bounce) are applied inside . This avoids double-modulation (albedo^2 x light at runtime) and keeps the lightmap free of the texel's diffuse-texture noise.

remarks.para: Direct: is deterministic with the current set of light types (point / directional / spot: no area lights yet, so no soft shadows), so the answer is the same regardless of .
Indirect: cosine-weighted hemisphere sampling via the precomputed ; throughput starts at 1 and picks up hit albedos only at bounce points.

member.name: T:XEngine.Photonic.Raytracing.Blas
member.summary: Per-mesh acceleration structure. We build a binary SAH BVH, collapse it into a wider BVH4 where each node stores 4 children's AABBs in SoA Vector128 lanes, and pad every leaf to exactly 4 triangles in SoA storage. Per node visit we do one SIMD ray-vs-4-AABB; per leaf visit we do one SIMD ray-vs-4-triangle test (Möller-Trumbore). Padding triangles are degenerate (E1 = E2 = 0) so the SIMD test rejects them automatically.

member.name: T:XEngine.Photonic.Raytracing.Blas.Node4
member.summary: BVH4 node: SoA AABB packs (lane i = child i) plus child / prim arrays. Inner children store a node index in C{i}; leaves store the 4-aligned first triangle index, with P{i} > 0 marking it as a leaf.

member.summary: Triangle vertex indices + material group. Looked up at hit time for material info.

member.name: P:XEngine.Photonic.Raytracing.Blas.Triangles
member.summary: Triangle reference array (parallel to the SoA edge arrays). Indices are padded so leaves occupy exactly 4 contiguous slots; padded slots have I0=I1=I2=0.

SIMD Möller-Trumbore against (= 8 with AVX2) triangles starting at . Returns per-lane (t, u, v) and a bitmask of which lanes hit (within tMin..maxT). Padding triangles have E1 = E2 = 0, so |det| is zero and they're naturally rejected.
